input.source:
Recording booth. This is a discrete spatial training game, not real equipment. Use these exact stable identifiers.
The room is an open 6 by 3 grid with no obstacles. The actor engineer starts at (1,1). Station recordPad is at (2,1), station archivePad at (4,1), marker approach at (3,1), and the locked object archiveDoor at (5,1).
The only station action is activate, performed by engineer. It is effective only from a cardinally adjacent cell (Manhattan distance exactly 1). Walk actions move the actor to a chosen marker; distant activation has no effect.
Initially archiveDoor is locked, flags started and clipped are false, and timer window is stopped at zero. The timer declaration has a capacity of 280 ticks.
An effective activation of recordPad, while not started, not clipped, and still locked, sets started to true and starts timer window.
The started timer runs for exactly 14 seconds.
An effective activation of archivePad unlocks archiveDoor and stops the timer only if started is true, clipped is false, the object is still locked, and the timer is still running.
At timer expiration, if started is true, clipped is false and the object remains locked, set clipped to true. Expiration takes precedence over an activation at exactly the expiration tick.
Activating archivePad before recordPad has no effect. Repeated activation of recordPad never restarts the timer. Once unlocked or failed, neither outcome can be reversed and no action restarts the process. There is no separate terminal win/lose action; the observation clock keeps running.
One second is 20 ticks. All positions and timer rules above are part of the source, not layout assumptions.
input.intervention: Experiment with a 5-second timer instead of 14 seconds. Keep the original source and all other rules. Compare the same visitor actions in both branches.
